prompt: A conjugated enone (α,β-unsaturated ketone) shows its C=O IR band around 1680 cm⁻¹, LOWER than a non-conjugated ketone at ~1715. Why?

options.label: Conjugation delocalizes the C=O π electrons across the enone system, reducing C=O bond order (partial double-bond character) and lowering the force constant → lower frequency.

explanation: Conjugation (C=C adjacent to C=O) delocalizes the π system. The C=O gains some single-bond character (electrons spread to C=C). Weaker effective C=O bond → lower stretching frequency by ~30 cm⁻¹. This is diagnostic: if C=O is unusually LOW (~1680), suspect conjugation.
